ai.description: This 6–12 cm frog is bright green above with a pale yellow belly. It features a pointed snout, fully webbed toes, and distinct longitudinal skin folds along its back.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Indian Green Frog (*Euphlyctis hexadactyla*) is best distinguished by the prominent, bright yellow coloration on the underside of its thighs and groin area.
ai.habitat: The Indian Green Frog inhabits permanent freshwater bodies like ponds, marshes, and lakes, typically below 1,000m, where it thrives amidst dense floating aquatic vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Indian Green Frog is primarily nocturnal and aquatic, often remaining submerged with only its eyes and nostrils above the water to ambush passing insects and fish.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Euphlyctis hexadactyla* is an oviparous breeder that spawns throughout the year, peaking during monsoons. Females lay large clutches of up to 5,000 eggs in stagnant water.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Green Frog is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, occurring from lowlands up to 1,000 meters in various freshwater habitats.
ai.callDescription: The Indian Green Frog emits a loud, rhythmic "chuck-chuck" call with a low pitch, typically heard from permanent water bodies like ponds and marshes.
